criteria.criterion: Fixes finding 1 (major) of job 20261111-055238-5har: the section on host main moving and two jobs landing at once does not claim a push refusal. It states, citing Git::push_branch in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs (about lines 430-436) that a plain push to a new PR branch is refused only when the branch exists and is not a descendant, so a main move does not fail the push. It names the real detection point: the host merge (gh/client.rs MergeMethod) preceded by an is_ancestor check that the PR's parent is still the main tip (or a host up-to-date requirement), then refetch and rebuild with merge_tree, with a concrete failure signal per case.
criteria.evidence: Section 7 cites push_branch at lines 430-436. Read confirms lines 430-436 hold push_branch, and its doc comment says the push is refused only when the branch exists and the commit does not descend from it. The note says a main move never fails the push. It places detection just before the host merge (MergeMethod at client.rs:416), using Git::is_ancestor and an equality check, with the up-to-date setting as an option. The moved-main case refetches, runs merge_tree, runs commit_tree and pushes under a fresh name. Signals are given for: parent still the tip, main moved, host refuses, and two jobs at once.

findings.summary: The note says the host refuses the merge if main moves between the pre-merge check and the merge call. That is not guaranteed.
findings.evidence: gh/client.rs merge (around line 688) sends only `sha` (the PR head) and `merge_method`. The host refuses when the head moved, not when the base moved. Without the optional up-to-date branch setting or a real conflict, a PR built on an old tip merges cleanly. The two-jobs bullet hedges with '(or the up-to-date requirement)', but the 'host refuses' bullet states the error as fact. The fix is to say that this narrow window is closed only by the up-to-date setting or a conflict, and is otherwise a clean merge of non-conflicting content.
findings.location: docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md section 7, 'Signal when the host refuses the merge anyway' and 'Two jobs land at once'

findings.summary: The moved-main check is worded redundantly.
findings.evidence: The decision is just 'fetched tip == PR parent'. Describing it as 'is_ancestor(fetched_tip, parent) false, or the tip differs from the parent' adds a call that the equality test already covers. Stating the equality test alone would be simpler.

summary: The candidate fixes all three findings from job 20261111-055238-5har, and only docs change. Finding 1: the race section no longer claims a push refusal. It quotes Git::push_branch correctly (lib.rs lines 430-436), says a push to a new branch never fails when main moves, and puts detection before the host merge (gh/client.rs MergeMethod) with an is_ancestor or equality check, followed by a refetch and merge_tree rebuild. Each case has its own failure signal. Finding 2: the 5.0-minute prediction is now scored only against the verifier-to-first-record stage, which is about 4.6 minutes by the note's own figures. The note says the headline 2984.3 median is not the figure compared with 5.0, and it requires the implementing change to cite the review. Finding 3: the roadmap uses plain numbering 4 and 5, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry. I checked the note's code citations against the code: merge_tree, commit_tree, push_branch, fetch_remote_branch, is_ancestor and merge_tree_report; land.rs dispatched_from, refuse_detached, plan with merge_tree(p, head, c), resync_onto_merge and the fingerprint stale check; gh/landing.rs land_pr, publish, plan_rebase, rebase_job_branch and close_carried_prs. All exist as described. I also checked the figures against the evidence snapshot: 2984.3 and 2990.6 in the review record, 28.5 in the earlier request text, and 4.6, 60 of 215, 2252.0 and the earlier stage medians in the existing notes. All match. Two small accuracy problems remain, neither blocking: the note says the host returns an error if main moves between the check and the merge call, and the ancestry check is worded redundantly.
